title: Quaestiones super secundo libro magistri sententarium
shelf_note: No tradition or collection assigned. It is a 13th/14th-c. scholastic commentary on Book II of Lombard's Sentences (angels, illumination, the Fall), which belongs among medieval theology sources.
structure_note: 438 pages, 415 with OCR, 394 translated. All three leaves sit in sequence (folio numbers x.xxij, x.xxxvj on the image), and the page-level coverage gap is plausible for blanks and flyleaves. The OCR's own <page-num> misreads the folio (X.XXV. vs x.xxij on p.225; f. xxxij vs x.xxxvj on p.329).

title: De bello Turcico
shelf_note: No tradition or collection assigned. It is a 1572 neo-Latin epic on Lepanto, early modern Latin literature and not core esoteric material, but nothing makes it wrong for the library.
structure_note: 45 images, all OCR'd and translated. Each image is a two-page opening (running head LIBER | PRIMVS split across the spread), and the OCR handles it as two columns, so no text is lost. The script is tagged 'handwritten', but this is the calligraphic italic of the edition, which may be engraved or written; it does no harm.

tr_errors.english: <gloss>St. John, likely referring to a galley of the Knights of Malta</gloss>

book_verdict: The transcription of this clean calligraphic edition is excellent. The translation is serviceable on the logistics pages but scrambles the battle narrative on p.34: who attacked whom, who helped whom, and three ships turned into one. A reader following Lepanto would be misled.

title: Bible in Latin with the prefaces of Jerome
shelf_note: No tradition assigned. It is a 13th-c. Vulgate, a core primary source.
structure_note: Only 21 images of a full Bible: the leaves carry manuscript page numbers 156, 205 and 255 and open Chronicles, Judith and Proverbs. The record is a selection of decorated openings, not a whole book. The title should say so.

title: Alchemical Texts annotated by John Dee (Trinity College O.2.47)
shelf_note: A 15th-c. alchemical miscellany (Latin and Middle English) with Dee provenance, squarely on the alchemy shelf.
structure_note: 116 images, all with OCR, 104 translated. The book language is Latin, but p.30 is Middle English (tagged correctly at page level), so this is a mixed-language miscellany. The leaf numerals 25 and 39 on the images fit the sequence.
